Indicator Question: The independent oversight body has the necessary mandate and power to perform its functions, including to review classified documents and inspect the premises of public bodies.
Indicator Desription:
To meet this benchmark, the oversight body must have the mandate and power to:

1) review classified documents;
2) inspect the premises of public bodies.

Oversight bodies that meet only one of the two criteria receive a Partial score.

Indicator Question: Everyone (including non-citizens and legal entities) has the right to file requests.
Indicator Desription:
To meet this benchmark, the following groups must be able to file requests for information:

1) all natural persons;
2) all legal persons.

Countries that meet only one of the two criteria receive a Partial score. If only residents/citizens may file requests, no points are given.

Indicator Title: Information is provided at a reasonable cost
Indicator Question: Access fees have clear, centrally-set rules, and are limited to the cost of reproducing and sending information, with some information provided for free.
Indicator Desription:
To meet this benchmark, access fee rules must:

1) be set centrally, rather than by individual public authorities;
2) require that fees be limited to the cost of reproducing and sending information (so that inspection of documents and electronic copies are free)
3) require that a certain initial number of pages (at least 20) be provided for free.

Access fees that meet only some of these criteria receive a Partial score.

Indicator Title: Requesters can appeal to an independent oversight body
Indicator Question: Requesters have the right to lodge an (external) appeal with an independent administrative oversight body (e.g. an information commission or ombudsman).

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: The oversight body is protected from political interference
Indicator Question: The oversight body reports to and has its budget approved by parliament, and its member(s) are protected from political interference and dismissal

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: The oversight body's decisions are binding
Indicator Question: The decisions of the independent oversight body are binding.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: The oversight body has investigative powers
Indicator Question: The independent oversight body has the necessary mandate and power to perform its functions, including to review classified documents and inspect the premises of public bodies.
Indicator Desription:
To meet this benchmark, the oversight body must have the mandate and power to:

1) review classified documents;
2) inspect the premises of public bodies.

Oversight bodies that meet only one of the two criteria receive a Partial score.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: The oversight body can order the declassification of information
Indicator Question: In deciding an appeal, the independent oversight body has the power to order appropriate remedies for the requester, including the declassification of information.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: Everyone has the right to file requests for information
Indicator Question: Everyone (including non-citizens and legal entities) has the right to file requests.
Indicator Desription:
To meet this benchmark, the following groups must be able to file requests for information:

1) all natural persons;
2) all legal persons.

Countries that meet only one of the two criteria receive a Partial score. If only residents/citizens may file requests, no points are given.

Indicator Title: Reasonable timelines exist for responding to requests
Indicator Question: Reasonable timelines exist for responding to requests

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: Information is provided at a reasonable cost
Indicator Question: Access fees have clear, centrally-set rules, and are limited to the cost of reproducing and sending information, with some information provided for free.
Indicator Desription:
To meet this benchmark, access fee rules must:

1) be set centrally, rather than by individual public authorities;
2) require that fees be limited to the cost of reproducing and sending information (so that inspection of documents and electronic copies are free)
3) require that a certain initial number of pages (at least 20) be provided for free.

Access fees that meet only some of these criteria receive a Partial score.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: Exceptions require a harm test before refusal
Indicator Question: A harm test applies to all exceptions, so that it is only where disclosure poses a risk of actual harm to a protected interest that it may be refused.
Indicator Desription: To meet this benchmark, a harm test must apply to all exceptions. Legal frameworks with up to three exceptions not subject to a harm test receive a Partial score. If four or more exceptions are not subject to a harm test, no points are given.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: Information must be disclosed when in the public interest
Indicator Question: There is a mandatory public interest override so that information must be disclosed where this is in the overall public interest, even if this may harm a protected interest.
Indicator Desription: To meet this benchmark, the public interest override must not be subject to overarching limitations or apply to only some exceptions. It must also be mandatory. For example, there are ‘hard’ overrides (which apply absolutely), such as for information about human rights, corruption or crimes against humanity.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: The framework applies to all parts of the executive branch
Indicator Question: The right of access applies to the executive branch, with no bodies or classes of information excluded.
Indicator Desription: This includes the executive (cabinet) and administration including all ministries, departments, local government, public schools, public health care bodies, the police, the armed forces, security services, and bodies owned or controlled by the above. Any exempted central agency (such as the armed forces, police, or archives) results in a Partial score.

Data Producer: Centre for Law and Democracy; Access Info Europe
Indicator Title: The framework applies to the legislative and judicial branches
Indicator Question: The right of access applies to the legislative and judicial branch, with no bodies or classes of information excluded.
Indicator Desription: This includes both administrative documents and other information at all levels of government. Frameworks that apply only to part of either branch receive a Partial score.
